On a calm lake, there is a small boat moving at a constant speed of $v_{0} = 1  \mathrm{m/s}$. The total mass of the person and the boat is $M = 200  \mathrm{kg}$, and the boat carries $N = 20$ identical small balls, each with a mass of $m = 5  \mathrm{kg}$. The person stands at the bow of the boat and throws a ball horizontally in the direction of the boat's motion at regular intervals. The resistance of water and air is negligible.

1. If each time the ball is thrown with a velocity of $v=6\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ relative to the shore, calculate the speed $v_{1}$ of the boat after the first ball is thrown and determine after how many balls the boat's velocity reverses direction?
2. If each time the ball is thrown with a velocity $v=6\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ relative to the boat, by how much will the speed of the boat change when the 16th ball is thrown?

raw_record.original_question:
On a calm lake, there is a small boat moving at a constant speed of $v_{0} = 1 \mathrm{m/s}$. The total mass of the person and the boat is $M = 200 \mathrm{kg}$, and the boat carries $N = 20$ identical small balls, each with a mass of $m = 5 \mathrm{kg}$. The person stands at the bow of the boat and throws a ball horizontally in the direction of the boat's motion at regular intervals. The resistance of water and air is negligible.

1. If each time the ball is thrown with a velocity of $v=6\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ relative to the shore, calculate the speed $v_{1}$ of the boat after the first ball is thrown and determine after how many balls the boat's velocity reverses direction?
2. If each time the ball is thrown with a velocity $v=6\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ relative to the boat, by how much will the speed of the boat change when the 16th ball is thrown?

Image description: In the figure, a small boat is on the water surface, and the dashed line represents the calm water surface; on the left side of the boat there are several identical small balls and they are labeled m, and the hull is labeled M = Mperson + Mboat; at the right end of the boat, a person stands at the bow and throws a small ball horizontally to the right; the arrow v0 above points to the right, indicating that the initial velocity of the boat is to the right. No horizontal external force is shown in the figure, so conservation of momentum in the horizontal direction can be used.

Take the original direction of motion of the boat as the positive direction. It is known that v0 = 1 m/s, M = 200 kg, N = 20, m = 5 kg.

1. If the velocity of each ball relative to the shore after being thrown is v = 6 m/s, then the initial total momentum is (M + Nm)v0. After k balls are thrown, each of the k thrown balls moves with shore speed v, and the mass of the remaining boat, person, and balls is M + (N-k)m, with velocity u_k. Conservation of momentum:
(M + Nm)v0 = [M + (N-k)m]u_k + kmv.
First ball throwing k = 1:
u_1 = [(M + Nm)v0 - mv] / [M + (N-1)m]
= [(200 + 20×5)×1 - 5×6] / [200 + 19×5]
= (300 - 30) / 295
= 270/295 m/s.
The condition for the boat to reverse direction is u_k < 0, that is, the numerator (M + Nm)v0 - kmv < 0:
300 - 30k < 0, so k > 10. Therefore after the 10th ball the boat's velocity is exactly 0, and after the 11th ball is thrown the boat reverses direction.

2. If the velocity of each ball relative to the boat after being thrown is v = 6 m/s. Before the kth ball is thrown, the system mass is M + (N-k+1)m, and the boat speed is u_{k-1}; after the ball is thrown, the mass of the boat and remaining balls is M + (N-k)m, the boat speed is u_k, and the velocity of the thrown ball relative to the shore is u_k + v. Conservation of momentum:
[M + (N-k+1)m]u_{k-1} = [M + (N-k)m]u_k + m(u_k + v).
After arranging, we get:
[M + (N-k+1)m](u_{k-1} - u_k) = mv,
so the magnitude of the change in boat speed when the kth ball is thrown is
Delta u_k = mv / [M + (N-k+1)m].
When the 16th ball is thrown:
Delta u_16 = 5×6 / [200 + (20 - 16 + 1)×5]
= 30 / 225
= 2/15 m/s.
